comparator.name: Econometrics and Data Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 pathway totals 180 EC: ten compulsory 6 EC courses in each of Years 1 and 2, 30 EC open study, three selected 6 EC subjects from seven, and a 12 EC thesis. The retained electives are Econometrics III, Machine Learning for Econometrics and Data Science, and Fair, Transparent and Interpretable Machine Learning; they are choices, not universal requirements. There is no formal graduation route. Teaching is English, with Dutch tutorial/expression/exam-answer options in Years 1–2. BSA requires 42 first-year EC, a pass in Calculus/Analysis I OR Analysis II/Mathematical Reasoning AND a pass in Introduction to Data Science OR Statistics. The English diagnostic or refresher gates Data Analysis I. Zero-credit BRIDGE requires attendance at five of six plenaries. Data Science Practical requires a final Data Structures and Algorithms grade of at least 5.5, or a first-period partial grade of at least 5.5 in Econometrics I or Numerical Methods. Thesis entry requires120EC including minor and at least two passes from Econometrics II, Multivariate Statistics and Data Science Methods. The thesis is individual quantitative research with a paper and poster/presentation, assessed by supervisor and second reader; topics appear in Period4. The current July2027 diploma deadline concerns current final-year students, not the future Fall2026 entrant’s Year3. The minor normally requires90EC; open study has at most6EC level100, at least12EC level300 and no compulsory-course overlap. Prior board approval applies except stated faculty/university/Education-minor exemptions; the Economics university minor is prohibited for EDS. Course manuals may require attendance. Honours is additional and excluded. Visible adopted OER AppendixVII schedule, version26-2-2026, is controlling; recruitment SAM and shortened elective list are outdated/incomplete. The annual Introduction to Data Science course is probability theory, not UCR-style data cleaning. Current year verified in each annual course page. No outgoing edition or guessed future deadline is used.

core: Calculus, linear algebra and mathematical reasoning
Probability, statistical inference and multivariate modelling
Programming, algorithms, databases and large-data handling
Econometric estimation and economic or business forecasting
Machine learning and data-science methods applied in projects
Ethics, fairness, privacy and interpretable data science
Macroeconomics and finance as quantitative application areas
Independent quantitative research and communicating results
adjacent: Marketing measurement, consumer demand and business decisions
questions: How can statistical and machine-learning models forecast economic outcomes such as inflation and consumer demand?
How can data estimate advertising effects and inform business decisions?
How can machine-learning decisions be made fair and interpretable?

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
trace: Mandatory first-year personal, academic and collaborative development; not quantitative thesis training.
Develops financial-statement analysis, costing and budgeting. Investment appraisal uses cash-flow discounting, payback and cost of capital.
Examines AI effects on competitiveness, innovation, labor, growth and corporate governance/fairness across business functions; supports critical organisational use of analytics, not technical ML.
Introduces microeconomic markets/consumer and firm behavior plus macroeconomic output, inflation and unemployment, providing economic interpretation for data analysis.
Develops macroeconomic dynamics, policy, growth, crises and trade; supplies economic interpretation for inflation and business-cycle questions, not econometric time-series estimation.
Analyzes consumer choice under uncertainty, preferences, imperfect competition and market efficiency; provides substantive demand/firm theory for quantitative applications.
Teaches OLS, GLS and IV, inference and Monte Carlo simulations in Stata with an empirical paper; directly implements applied estimation and prediction, not Econometrics II/III.
Uses biases, heuristics, framing and experiments to explain economic choices; complements the interpretation of economic data rather than specialist forecasting.
Consumer psychology, trust, brand strategy and marketing plans supply the substantive consumer-engagement domain for the secondary analytics concept.
Plans and executes market research, collecting and analyzing customer evidence and reporting results; no guaranteed causal advertising-effect estimator.
Studies global business institutions, cross-border governance, responsibility and trade; a specific complement for business decisions and governance, not a data-science method.
Team venture development includes customer/market validation and business-model testing, connecting quantitative inquiry to evidenced consumer/business decisions.
Introductory research design, operationalisation, experiments, surveys, sampling and inference with a group project; not full multivariate or mathematical-statistics training.
Philosophical and psychological AI ethics addresses fairness, bias, privacy and responsibility; it does not teach formal differential privacy or model-agnostic interpretability algorithms.
AI planning under uncertainty and resource constraints is a specific computational-decision complement; not econometric or supervised-learning estimation.
Discrete mathematics, logic and structures support algorithm construction and mathematical reasoning; not a substitute for Analysis II.
Implements search, constraints, first- and second-order optimization, and linear and discrete optimization for computational problems.
Implements reinforcement-learning algorithms and neural-network agents learning by trial and error; extends computational learning beyond supervised modeling.
Relational database theory, SQL, normalisation, authorization and queries directly support structured data management.
Algorithm design, data structures and experimental performance analysis with laboratory projects directly implement efficient computational methods.
Data cleaning, manipulation, visualisation and a research project support practical empirical analysis; unlike VU’s identically named probability course.
Regression/classification, resampling, shrinkage, trees, support vector machines and clustering implement statistical learning with real-data applications.
Builds and trains neural networks in Python/TensorFlow, then computer-vision/text models; specialised empirical deep learning rather than generalisation-risk proofs.
Python programming, data constructs, debugging and object-oriented problem solving provide the computational foundation.
Differentiation, integration, complex numbers and differential equations support quantitative methods; does not establish the full proof-based Analysis I/II sequence.
Linear equations, matrices, vector spaces, transformations and eigenvalues support multivariate quantitative reasoning.
Root finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation/integration and ODE algorithms develop accuracy/stability-aware numerical computation.
Linear time-invariant signals, convolution and Fourier/Laplace/Z transforms contribute systems mathematics; not state-space econometrics or economic time-series forecasting.
Probability, distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation provide mathematical statistics foundations for later modelling.

alternatives.label: Econometrics, machine learning and economic analysis
alternatives.concept: Studies economic questions through mathematics, programming, statistical learning and econometrics. Students build models, analyse economic data and study how markets, inflation and behaviour shape the results. Accounting and signals analysis add ways to interpret financial statements and work with mathematical systems.
alternatives.labelReason: Mathematics and computing support applied econometrics, statistical learning and economic interpretation.
progression: Programming, data analysis and logic begin in term one. Year-one mathematical methods and research statistics precede linear algebra, probability, numerical methods, machine learning and empirical econometrics. Optimization comes in term six.

alternatives.label: Consumer and marketing data analysis
alternatives.concept: Uses statistical learning and econometrics to investigate consumer and business questions. Students study consumer choice, practise market research and consider how firms use data and AI. The option includes collecting and interpreting market evidence and communicating results.
alternatives.labelReason: Marketing, market research and business courses focus the shared modelling sequence on consumer and organisational decisions.
progression: Programming, mathematics, business foundations, introductory data analysis and research methods precede databases, consumer study, machine learning and advanced market research and econometrics. Optimization comes in term six.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses differ in each direction (37.5 EC). Business foundations, consumer engagement, market research, business and AI, and international business replace accounting, discrete mathematics, signals analysis, reinforcement learning and behavioural economics.

candidates.label: Consumer demand, advertising and business analytics
Fair, responsible and interpretable machine learning

selection.assessment: Two options retain the shared quantitative core and differ in their application focus. Fair and responsible machine learning is supported in both through AI Ethics and modelling, while the available courses do not sustain a third distinct sequence in technical fairness, interpretability or privacy.

blocks: Both use differentiation and integration to analyse mathematical problems. VU also develops proof-based analysis.
Both develop data preparation, visualisation and analysis through practical work. VU adds an oral defence.
Both build programs in Python and develop computational problem-solving skills.
Both work with vectors, matrices, linear transformations and eigenvalues.
UCR develops mathematical reasoning in calculus and linear algebra. VU teaches a second dedicated analysis and proof course.
Both use probability distributions, estimation and statistical inference. UCR also studies mathematical statistics and simulation.
UCR covers probability and inference across mathematics and research methods. VU gives them a dedicated academic-skills course.
Both study data structures, algorithm design and computational efficiency.
Both develop numerical solutions for equations, interpolation and integration and consider accuracy and stability.
Both design relational databases and use SQL to query data.
UCR uses regression and statistical learning across several courses. VU gives multivariate statistics a dedicated course.
Both build statistical learning models and assess prediction. UCR covers regression, classification, resampling, trees and clustering.
Despite the title, this VU course introduces probability theory. UCR’s similarly named course focuses on preparing, exploring and visualising data.
Both evaluate investment projects using discounted cash flow and cost of capital. VU also values traded assets and builds investment portfolios.
Both estimate economic relationships and assess statistical evidence. UCR applies regression, instrumental variables and simulation in an empirical paper.
VU builds a second required econometrics course on its introductory methods. UCR offers one applied econometrics course.
VU offers advanced econometric theory and methods as a final-year choice. UCR has no comparable third econometrics course.
Both use macroeconomic models to examine output, inflation and policy. UCR also studies growth, crises and open economies.
VU requires a supervised data science practical. UCR uses practical projects across several courses.
Both examine ethical problems raised by data and AI. UCR covers bias, privacy and responsibility through ethical analysis.
VU requires an integrated data science project. UCR applies similar skills within its computing and data courses.
VU reserves 30 EC for a minor or approved elective study. The UCR schedules show a complete course selection.
VU requires an individual quantitative thesis and poster. UCR offers optional independent research outside the displayed schedules.
UCR discusses bias and responsibility in AI Ethics. The VU elective teaches technical fairness and interpretability methods.
UCR builds and evaluates learning models. The VU elective adds a theoretical treatment of learning and generalisation.

notes.text: VU requires a longer econometrics sequence, dedicated multivariate statistics, integrated practicals and a 12 EC thesis. It also offers technical electives in learning theory, fairness and privacy. UCR provides related modelling and economic analysis, with optional independent research outside the schedules.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Amsterdam combines economics, mathematics, statistics and computing. Students estimate economic relationships, analyse data, study responsible use of data and complete a quantitative thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers two ways to study related questions. One combines economic analysis, econometrics and machine learning. The other uses the shared quantitative foundation to study consumer behaviour and market research.

curriculum.limitation: The final year includes 30 EC of elective study, three choices from seven subjects and a 12 EC thesis. Thesis entry requires at least 120 EC and passes in two of Econometrics II, Multivariate Statistics and Data Science Methods.
